bib.title: UniversalRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Corpora of Diverse Modalities and Granularities

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "UniversalRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Corpora of Diverse Modalities and Granularities", Woongyeong Yeo* and Kangsan Kim* (equal first authors; Yeo listed first), Soyeong Jeong, Jinheon Baek, Sung Ju Hwang (KAIST, DeepAuto.ai). arXiv:2504.20734, version v5 dated 12 Jun 2026. No venue is stated, so treat it as a preprint (cs.CL). The PDF is a later revision than the 2025 filename suggests, and the models in it are 2025-26 (Qwen3-VL, GPT-5, Molmo2).

COVERAGE: 122,426 of 122,426 chars extracted, 33 pages. I read the body, limitations, Tables 1-5, and appendix A, B and C (partly), D, E, F text. In C I read only C.1 and the C.3 conclusion; C.2 and the F case-study tables 11-14 are only skimmed. The reference list was skimmed. pypdf warned "Exceeded 5000 form XObject invocations", so some figure-internal content is skipped. Figures were not rendered.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Merging all modalities into one embedding space causes a modality gap. Retrieval favours items of the query's own modality (text), so cross-modal evidence is missed.
  number: none for the principle. Measured effect: unified encoders retrieve almost only text (Fig 4), and modality accuracy is at or near chance (Table 3).
  setup: 200 sampled queries per benchmark; VLM2Vec-V2, GME and UniversalRAG (Qwen3-VL-2B router); 10 benchmarks.
  quote: "VLM2Vec-V2 retrieves exclusively text, while GME similarly exhibits a strong bias toward text regardless of the query's required modality"
  where: p7, Effectiveness of Modality Routing.
- Route first, then retrieve inside the chosen per-modality corpus. Each corpus keeps its own index and embedding space, so no cross-modality comparison happens. The router also lets you add a modality without touching the existing retrievers.
  number: none
  setup: method design, section 2.2.
  quote: "this strategy not only sidesteps modality gaps by avoiding every cross-modal comparison but also enables seamless integration of new modalities by extending the routing logic without modifying existing modality-specific retrievers."
  where: p2.
- Router modality accuracy, and the effect on recall.
  number: modality accuracy 95.28 (Qwen3-VL-2B trained), 92.39 (InternVL3.5-1B), 68.22 (GPT-5 training-free), 36.27 (GME), 25.00 (UniRAG, PEcore, VLM2Vec-V2). R@1 / R@3 / R@5 of 21.38 / 36.29 / 44.82 for the Qwen3-VL-2B router, against 2.30 / 3.69 / 4.12 for VLM2Vec-V2.
  setup: Table 3 (a mixed multimodal retrieval set).
  quote: "UniversalRAG(Qwen3-VL-2B)95.28 21.38 36.29 44.82" and "VLM2Vec-V2 25.00 2.30 3.69 4.12"
  where: p6, Table 3.
- Average end-to-end score. UniversalRAG with a 2B trained router beats every baseline. It is near the oracle router and well above the best fixed single-corpus RAG.
  number: Avg 42.40 (Qwen3-VL-2B router), 42.12 (InternVL3.5-1B), 39.26 (GPT-5 training-free), 39.46 (Qwen3-VL-8B training-free). Oracle is 42.45. Baselines: ParagraphRAG 37.26, Naive 35.59, MultiRAG 34.07, GME 33.88.
  setup: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct generator; 10 benchmarks, mixed metrics (Acc, EM/F1, ROUGE-L, BERTScore) averaged; 3:7 train/test split.
  quote: "UniversalRAG (Ours) ... Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct 74.39 38.65 50.61 ... 42.40" and "Oracle 74.39 39.25 51.32 ... 42.45"
  where: p5, Table 1. Table 8 (p23) repeats the pattern with InternVL3.5-8B and Molmo2-4B.
- The gain over fixed-source baselines comes from picking the right source. A mismatched fixed corpus does much worse than the matched one. Retrieving from all corpora (MultiRAG) adds noise and is worse than routing.
  number: Avg 34.07 for MultiRAG against 42.40. Example: HotpotQA EM is 26.35 for DocumentRAG against 21.10 for Naive; on NQ, TableRAG gets 11.80 EM.
  setup: Table 1, Qwen3-VL-8B generator.
  quote: "mismatches between the query and retrieval source results in significant degradation" and "which results in suboptimal performance due to the inclusion of noise from irrelevant modalities in generation"
  where: p7.
- Granularity-aware routing. Choosing paragraph or document, or clip or video, helps over a single granularity. Gains are not strictly monotonic as levels are added.
  number: GPT-5 router HotpotQA EM 23.20 (1 level), 24.35 (2), 24.20 (3), 24.70 (4). Trained routers: Qwen3-VL-2B HotpotQA EM 22.25 without granularity, 26.10 with; LVBench accuracy 32.05 without, 33.72 with.
  setup: Tables 4 and 9. HotpotQA is document-level (multi-hop); LVBench is video. The main experiments use only 2 levels.
  quote: "gains are not strictly monotonic across tasks, reflecting the trade-off between context sufficiency and noise"
  where: p7-8 and p24.
- Cross-modal routing (more than one corpus per query) beats a single chosen modality.
  number: HybridQA EM/F1 11.05/16.23 cross-modal against 9.60/14.56 uni-modal (Qwen3-VL-2B). GPT-5: 4.95/8.79 against 4.75/8.57.
  setup: Table 2; HybridQA (table+text) and WebQA (text+image).
  quote: "Qwen3-VL-2B Uni-modal 9.60 14.56 67.93 95.58Cross-modal11.05 16.23 70.22 95.86"
  where: p6.
- Trained routers win in-domain but degrade out of domain. The training-free GPT-5 router generalizes better. Ensembling the two gives a balance.
  number: In-domain router accuracy 95.81 (Qwen3-VL-2B) against 72.33 (GPT-5). Out-of-domain accuracy 71.29 against 77.38. Ensemble (confidence-based) 96.02 in-domain and 80.71 out-of-domain; majority vote 98.33 and 78.56. Random routing is 14.29.
  setup: 6 OOD datasets (TruthfulQA, TriviaQA, SQuAD, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Visual-RAG, CinePile); Table 5. The trained router's labels are derived automatically from the benchmarks.
  quote: "Ensemble(Confidence-based)96.02 42.53 80.71 44.71"
  where: p8, Table 5.
- Small routers suffice, and routing cuts latency at scale.
  number: a 1B router gets "approximately 90% accuracy". Latency is sub-linear in corpus size from 100k to 100M entries, and "eventually" below a unified index, with the gap widening beyond 10M entries. Fig 5 data points are not extractable.
  setup: Fig 5 and Fig 6; T5Gemma 2 270M router; router sizes from 256M to 4B.
  quote: "a 1B-parameter model attains approximately 90% accuracy, indicating that compact models can serve as effective routers"
  where: p8.
- Theory. Under a unified index, if the modality bias alpha is large relative to the variance of relevance, the chance of retrieving from the required modality is lower than with routing. Latency is T_unified = T(kN) against T_routing = C + T(N), assuming parallel retrieval and a linear-scaling backend.
  number: none (the ratio is roughly k / (1 + C/N))
  setup: Proposition 2.1 / C.1 uses independent, sub-Gaussian, mean-zero score noise (a toy model). C.3 assumes parallel calls.
  quote: "𝑠(𝑞,𝑐) =𝛼·1{𝑚(𝑞) =𝑚(𝑐)}+𝛽·𝑟(𝑞,𝑐) +𝜀"
  where: p4 and p21-22.

Implementation facts worth keeping
- Trained router: classifier head on an LVLM, multi-hot targets, binary cross-entropy, 5 epochs, lr 2e-5, LoRA r=32, sigmoid threshold 0.8. It returns all modality-granularity pairs above the threshold.
- Training-free router: Gemini-style prompt with few-shot examples (Fig 8).
- Seven routes: None, Paragraph, Document, Table, Image, Clip, Video.
- Paragraphs are at most 100 words. HotpotQA documents are grouped to over 4K tokens, following LongRAG. Clips are at most 3 minutes, cut with PySceneDetect, and 32 frames are sampled per video.
- Visual retrieval combines visual and text similarity with weight 0.8 on the visual part.
- Encoders: Qwen3-Embedding-4B for text, VLM2Vec-V2 for vision, row-level embeddings for tables.
- Router labels are assigned by inductive bias from each dataset (for example, NQ maps to Paragraph and HotpotQA to Document). This is a circularity risk.

LIMITS
- The authors concede there are no ground-truth routing labels. Labels are auto-annotated and noisy. Only 2 granularity levels (text and video) are used because annotations are lacking.
- Router quality is the central dependency. Training-free GPT-5 reaches only 68.22% modality accuracy in-domain (Table 3).
- Trained routers degrade OOD: 71.29 and 67.85 against 77.38 for GPT-5.
- My observations, not the authors' concessions:
  - Each benchmark maps almost one-to-one to a route, so in-domain trained-router accuracy is probably inflated.
  - Corpora are small and benchmark-specific (for example, 89 videos for LVBench, 6k to 20k items for the image sets).
  - Latency scaling is theory plus one plot, not measured at 100M entries.
  - Avg mixes incompatible metrics.
  - The table does not show the cost of the router call itself.
  - Evaluation covers LVLM-generated answers only, with no reranking or hybrid text retrieval baseline.

BUILDS ON: Lewis et al., 2020 (RAG); modality gap (Liang et al., 2022; Meng et al., 2026 / VLM2Vec-V2); Adaptive-RAG-style query-complexity routing (Jeong et al., 2024; the reference list is only skimmed, so this attribution is unverified); Dense X Retrieval granularity (Chen et al., 2024b, EMNLP 2024); LongRAG (Jiang et al., 2024b) for document grouping; Karpukhin et al., 2020 (DPR) for Wikipedia paragraphs; MuRAG (Chen et al., 2022); UniRAG (Sharifymoghaddam et al., 2025); GME (Zhang et al., 2025b); PE-core (Bolya et al., 2025); RAG-Anything (Guo et al., 2025) as an alternative that converts everything to text; VideoRAG (Jeong et al., 2025).

CODE: none in the paper. The router prompt is in Fig 8 and the granularity prompt in Fig 9 (appendix); I did not capture their text.

FIGURES (not rendered; captions from the extraction)
- Fig 1, p2: "Conceptual illustration comparing existing RAG strategies with our proposed UniversalRAG." It shows the router sending queries to the None, Paragraph, Document, Table, Image, Clip and Video corpora. Best single picture of the method.
- Fig 2 and Fig 7, p2 and p25: t-SNE and PCA of the unified embedding space, with points clustering by modality. Use these to show the modality gap.
- Fig 4, p6: distribution of retrieved modalities for Oracle, VLM2Vec-V2, GME and UniversalRAG. Unified encoders return nearly 100% text.
- Fig 5, p6: retrieval latency against corpus size from 100k to 100M entries.
- Fig 6, p6: router accuracy against parameter count.
- Fig 3, p5: averaged scores across the three generators.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Figure internals and the Fig 5 numbers are not extractable. Appendix text on Fig 8 and Fig 9 prompts and Tables 11-14 was not read in detail. Venue not stated in the PDF.

WHICH NOTE SECTION THE STRONGEST POINT BEARS ON
- The strongest point is routing to separate per-modality (and per-granularity) corpora instead of one shared embedding index. It is backed by the Table 3, Fig 4 and Table 5 numbers above.
- 11-retrieval-improvements.md is an ablation walkthrough of one text-only help-centre pipeline and has no router or modality content. The closest hooks are its regex-router versus LLM-planner line (about line 50: "LLM planner: -0.031 MRR against the regex router, and +4s latency") and its glossary-routing line near 469, which defers to 10 (semantic cache) for source routing. UniversalRAG counters that line: its LLM-router result is the opposite, in a multimodal setting.
- The better home is 07-rag-in-production.md, section "Multimodal RAG" (lines 472-486). Its table already lists "One shared space" and "Separate retrieval per modality", with the trade-offs "CLIP and multimodal LLMs cost more" and "Needs a multimodal reranker to merge the results". It does not state the modality-gap bias, and it presents separate retrieval as needing a reranker rather than a router. UniversalRAG sharpens that row with a measured bias and a router alternative to a merge reranker.
- 07 also has a router row at lines 332-340 (RAGate, skipping retrieval) and a router latency budget (~200 ms). The paper's "None" route and its small-router results (1B gives ~90% accuracy) sharpen that row.
- 01-rag-pipeline.md has the "Adaptive" pattern (#4) and a Text-to-SQL "needs a router, not a single index" paragraph (line 393). The paper supports that line's general point: the router is a first-class component and evaluating router accuracy matters.
- 05-chunking-query-parsing-and-reranking.md has no routing or granularity text by grep. The paper's granularity result (paragraph against document by query type, with HotpotQA multi-hop needing documents) bears on chunk size in 05 and on the small-to-big material in 01 (around line 408). I did not check those sections in depth.
- The note does not state the modality-gap finding. It does say routing in general and the router-accuracy-as-a-component idea. Treat the paper as sharpens for 07 Multimodal RAG (add the citation and references row), with a one-line cross-reference from 11 if wanted.
